site.name: NIP
site.tagline: An in-kernel protocol stack for Named Data Networking
site.description: NIP is a research site around iStack, documenting the design, implementation and evaluation of bringing Named Data Networking (NDN) into the OS kernel.

home.title: Bringing Named Data Networking into the OS kernel
home.intro: NDN forwards by name rather than address and keeps per-packet state in the data plane. iStack takes NDN into the OS kernel for the first time while staying compatible with the existing address-based stack and socket interfaces.
home.designIntro: Building a stateful, purely name-based stack in a general-purpose OS means solving name resolution, address abstraction and per-packet state together.
home.designNrsDesc: A name resolution architecture that serves both network-layer forwarding and local packet demultiplexing, keeping lookups on the kernel data path.
home.designFacesDesc: A two-layer face abstraction over address-based interfaces such as MAC, IP and port, so a name-based stack can coexist with the kernel network architecture.
home.designSocketDesc: Socket-compatible APIs preserve the way applications use the network stack, paired with compact forwarding data structures to keep the memory footprint low.
home.resourcesIntro: Read the docs for the system design, or go straight to the NSDI '24 paper and talk materials.
home.docsCardDesc: Condensed notes on motivation, architecture and evaluation.
home.blogCardDesc: Notes on NDN, in-kernel protocol stacks and stateful forwarding.
home.paperCardDesc: The official USENIX NSDI '24 page, PDF and presentation video.
